detail.longDescription: Hi HN, I've been building SaaS products for more than 20 years, and lately I've been thinking a lot about how we interact with software. When we add a feature, we have to figure out where it goes in the UI and how users will interact with it. Then users have to learn our particular way of doing something. AI lets us flip that around: the software can translate what the user wants into the actions needed to accomplish it. Yedric lets devs add a natural-language interface to an existing SaaS app. You expose your app's actions and give it your docs and user context. Users can then ask for things like: • "Export the table to a CSV" • "Fix this disconnected integration" • "Change my logo color to #B5E2F4" We originally built Yedric for our own Shopify apps and discovered an interesting side effect: the conversations became a useful source of product feedback. One of our apps surfaced 80+ distinct feature requests this way last month. Yedric uses a small JS SDK and MCP to connect to your app's capabilities. It's free, you bring your own LLM key, and you can get a basic implementation running in under 30 minutes. Let me know how you like it!
